coreIdea: A Tauri plugin crosses four independent locks—declared API, generated Rust-to-TypeScript bindings, runtime capability authority, and platform-native execution—and evidence for one lock cannot open the others.
analogies: The export ledger is the parts list: it proves what was shipped, not that the machine ran.
A capability is a keycard assigned to a webview: installing the plugin does not grant every command.
MockRuntime is a desktop fire drill; Android Kotlin and iOS Swift are different buildings and require their own drills.

skepticChallenges.challenge: The tarball contains Android and iOS sources, so mobile support is proven.
skepticChallenges.answer: Source presence proves packaging only. It does not prove native registration, serialization, capability evaluation, or the response path on either platform.

skepticChallenges.challenge: The desktop IPC test exercises the same command name, so mobile evidence is redundant.
skepticChallenges.answer: The command name is shared, but desktop executes Rust directly while mobile delegates through PluginHandle into Kotlin or Swift. The untested bridge is the feature under claim.

skepticChallenges.challenge: A persistSnapshot command proves restart durability.
skepticChallenges.answer: Names are not evidence. The current Rust state uses an in-memory map; durable SQLite remains the separate core adapter path.

transferProblems.problem: A new mutation command is added to Rust and generated TypeScript, but not the default permission set. What must change?
transferProblems.solution: Refresh the public declaration/runtime ledger, document the new explicit allow/deny permission, keep default read-only unless policy intentionally changes, and add denial plus allowed-host evidence.

transferProblems.problem: An Android cross-compile passes and the APK contains the Kotlin class. Can coverage mark mobile runtime implemented?
transferProblems.solution: No. Keep mobile runtime planned until a simulator or device invokes the command through the registered native bridge and records the exact response and denial artifact.

qualityGate.reason: Retention cannot be demonstrated in the same execution turn.
